title: Fundamentals of Generative AI - Week 11 Assignment 11
subject: Fundamentals of Generative AI

questions.question: 1. What is the primary motivation for using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?
options: To increase the number of parameters in the language model
To ground generated responses using external information retrieved
To replace tokenization with document retrieval
To eliminate the need for a language model
questions.correctAnswer: To ground generated responses using external information retrieved
questions.explanation: RAG reduces hallucinations and grounds responses by fetching factual, up-to-date context from an external corpus.

questions.question: 2. Which advantage does RAG provide when the underlying knowledge base changes frequently?
options: The entire language model must be retrained after every change
The tokenizer automatically learns the new information
The external index can be updated without retraining the model
The model permanently memorizes every retrieved document
questions.correctAnswer: The external index can be updated without retraining the model
questions.explanation: Knowledge bases can be dynamically updated, inserted, or removed from the vector database without retraining the foundational LLM.

questions.question: 3. Which sequence correctly describes a basic RAG pipeline?
options: Generation → Retrieval → Indexing → Chunking
Retrieval → Model training → Tokenization → Generation
Prompt construction → Chunking → Indexing → Retrieval
Document indexing → Query retrieval → Prompt augmentation → Response generation
questions.correctAnswer: Document indexing → Query retrieval → Prompt augmentation → Response generation
questions.explanation: The standard RAG lifecycle consists of Document indexing, Query retrieval, Prompt augmentation, and Response generation.

questions.question: 4. What is the primary role of the retriever in a RAG system?
options: To identify documents relevant to the user query
To generate the final natural-language response
To update all parameters of the language model
To select the decoding temperature
questions.correctAnswer: To identify documents relevant to the user query
questions.explanation: The retriever searches the index to identify and rank candidate documents relevant to the query.

questions.question: 5. What is the primary purpose of a vector database in a dense RAG pipeline?
options: To train the embedding model
To generate answers without using an LLM and bypassing it
To convert retrieved passages into labels
To store vector representations for similarity search
questions.correctAnswer: To store vector representations for similarity search
questions.explanation: Vector databases index dense embedding vectors to enable rapid approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) similarity search.

questions.question: 6. Why are long documents commonly divided into smaller chunks before indexing?
options: Language models can only retrieve complete documents
To allow retrieving more focused and relevant passages
Chunking increases the number of model parameters
Chunking removes the need for an embedding model
questions.correctAnswer: To allow retrieving more focused and relevant passages
questions.explanation: Chunking segments documents into semantically focused units that fit context windows and improve retrieval precision.

questions.question: 7. What is a major advantage of dense retrieval over purely lexical retrieval?
options: It does not require an indexed corpus
It can retrieve semantically related passages with different words
It guarantees that every retrieved document is correlated and correct
It does not require a similarity function
questions.correctAnswer: It can retrieve semantically related passages with different words
questions.explanation: Dense embeddings encode conceptual semantics, matching queries to documents that express similar ideas with different vocabulary.

questions.question: 8. What is the purpose of metadata filtering in document retrieval?
options: To modify the parameters of the embedding model
To summarize every document before retrieval
To restrict retrieval using irrelevant attributes
To replace semantic similarity with random selection
questions.correctAnswer: To restrict retrieval using irrelevant attributes
questions.explanation: Metadata filtering pre-filters or post-filters search space using structured attributes (such as dates, authors, categories, or tags).

questions.question: 9. What does Precision@k measure in a retrieval system?
options: The percentage of generated tokens copied from the documents
The average length of the top k documents
The Percentage of relevant documents in top k retrieved results
The time required to generate k responses
questions.correctAnswer: The Percentage of relevant documents in top k retrieved results
questions.explanation: Precision@k computes the fraction of relevant passages among the top-k retrieved items.

questions.question: 10. In a basic retrieve-then-generate system, how is retrieved information usually provided to the language model?
options: It is inserted into the prompt as additional context
It is used to replace the tokenizer vocabulary
It is converted into new trainable parameters
It is used only after the answer has been generated
questions.correctAnswer: It is inserted into the prompt as additional context
questions.explanation: Retrieved passages are formatted into the input prompt as supporting context for the generator.
